answer_1.quote: the problem of generating clarifying questions for open-domain conversations: the system must identify wherever the question is ambiguous, and, if so then instead of trying to answer it directly, it should ask a good clarifying question

answer_2.quote: We use Precision, Recall, F1-Measure, and Mean Squared Error (MSE). ... use the following standard metrics: Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), Precision (P)@[1,3,5,10,20], Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (nDCG)@[1,3,5,20] ... evaluated in terms of Recall@k

answer_4.quote: we conduct a pairwise human evaluation on two of the baselines. We use and extend the Acute-eval human annotation framework to evaluate 120 randomly sampled dialogue pairs.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked: 'Which one asks better (or more reasonable) clarifying questions?' and evaluated based on Humanness (HU), Engagingness (EG), Interestingness (IN), Knowledgeable (KL), and Clarification (CL).
